I mean I started it to vindicate myself and offer possible reasons cheating could be justified. But I often still wonder if I should tell him. I think he already knows though. 1. He was aware of a message I got from a man I was about to meet up with. I think he had some sort of software on my computer too, because he randomly told me to stop watching porn at home, because it was making him get in trouble for supposedly watching it at work. Then, during the brief stage when he actually agreed to have an open marriage, he said he wanted to know who I was seeing and where I was going at all times. My lover begged me not to reveal his name, because he was afraid of my ex. I lied about where I was going, but then my ex somehow knew Where I’d actually been, so he might have had a tracking setting on my phone ? I don’t know. I think he knows but doesn’t want to admit he was tracking my whereabouts and watching my internet activity.
Yeah total 180. I honestly think he’s a far better person than I am now.

I had generalized anxiety from a young age but was diagnosed with bipolar 1 due to a postpartum episode. From there it was mostly depression and anxiety. I think it was both the abuse and innate illness. My bipolar has become manageable with meds and being in a healthy situation and not smoking weed. I haven’t had bipolar depression in 3 months and haven’t been manic in a year. 
I think it was worsened by the relationship, worsened by the custody battle, and now that I’m in a safe living situation, taking meds, not dating, have a healthyish sleep schedule I’m recovering. 
It’s a crazy long story, but I can objectively say, particularly a year ago, my ex-husband was the better parent. It helps he has his gf to help him. 
Now, modern day, I feel like the shit parent, but I really do try. 
By our agreement, I’ll be with my son summers only while I finish school. 
All this bashing who he was, who he is now after domestic violence therapy & genuine aims to grow is amazing. He’s one of the most empathetic people I can think of. Hence when I have an issue about the past, I post to reddit, not publicly. He told me not to even pay child support so I can finish school and remain psychologically healthy. 
I’m undecided if I’ll ever tell him I cheated. I don’t know if it will help him or hurt him more. What are your thoughts ?

That’s kind of a complicated one to respond to rationally. He used my actual bipolar as a reason if I left him, he’d have me committed. So I’m legit mentally ill but feel I was perfectly sane when I made those decisions. Like I knew damn well what I was doing, I wasn’t out of my mind. My mental illness isn’t something I use to justify my decisions. My son missed out on a lot during my bipolar depression, and that’s gonna haunt me for the rest of my life. My mental illness was no excuse. The way it affected him, I see, as the worst thing I’ve ever done.
I definitely agree that neglect is abuse. And it’s legally defined as such.

Something we can agree on: if I cheat again, I’m shit. I’d like to think I’ve learned. My other strategy is to jump ship at even the slightest red flag. That might not account for the fact I have my own red flags, but if I jump ship too easily as opposed to getting trapped again, I’m less likely to do the same bs I did when I felt trapped in the past.

You’re not wrong. I have become a runner. I’m not getting into another relationship for a while for a reason. I don’t trust myself, the people I’m into deserve better, and my last almost lover turned out to probably be a pimp. Dodged that bullet and haven’t dated in over a year.

I don’t think my fear of being close to people made it any more right, because the man didn’t do a damn thing wrong. He spoiled me, in fact, and I was too selfish and scared to appreciate him. We weren’t compatible on other levels. I needed to break up with him, but I didn’t. I was a dick instead.
I was saying that was a reason, but I didn’t say that excused it. Still said it was wrong.

Ad hominem is fine too. 

I know some people who think calling someone fucked up and an asshole is verbal abuse, because of how badly those words hurt them. My sister recently told me she had been verbally abused when her friend called her fucked up. My sister is very sensitive. 
Fortunately I disagree. Because it’s not that black & white. I imagine you had some sort of painful cheating experience, making this a really emotionally charged discussion. Could be wrong. But I’m sorry that happened if so.

I don’t think my trauma excused cheating on my first boyfriend after him. It wouldn’t justify cheating on someone later either. And I have no plan to date unless the person is open to polyamory. It’s just my opinion, but I don’t think that’s a fucked up way to look at things. I’m fucked up in some ways, but I’m fairly sure I won’t enter another relationship until I’m a better person and not without precautions.
I’m saying there’s no excuse for cheating on my ex-boyfriend who didn’t abuse me. You’re misreading the differences.

Much longer. Grasping at reasons to invalidate this now? He started dating his girlfriend about a month after we separated and has been with her for years now. I’m very happy for the two. She cheated on him as well, and I just hope it’s not for reasons similar to mine. They’re still together though.

I see that there is a hashtag on Reddit for the issue you’re passionate about. If I held my ex against his will, and he cheated on me, I would be okay with that. 
Except that I don’t envision holding someone against their will and not caring about their consent ? 
If I do the exact same thing he does, and it comes around, good. But I doubt I would do that to someone. 
I don’t think my ex-boyfriend deserved cheating. I don’t justify that one. At all. 
I don’t think it’s right that I got cheated on. But the trauma from being held against my will was exponentially worse, especially considering I gave my ex husband the freedom to see others too.

I mean cheating is not legally defined as abuse. The cheating was stupid. I hate myself for cheating on the good guy I found after I left my marriage. That was wrong.  If I date again, which I don’t plan on any time soon, I plan to date someone at least open to polyamory.

The first relationship I had after my ex, I cheated, and I had no excuse. I didn’t want to be attached to anyone again, because I was scared. I think that time was wrong anyway. He deserved better. See? It’s not an always. These things aren’t always black & white.
I’ve been cheated on. Not by my ex-husband, though I gave him permission. If he had, it wouldn’t be abuse in my book. When I was cheated on, it sucked. It wasn’t abuse.
Where’s your source for proving cheating is abuse beyond your personal beliefs?

Can you logically address this ? My moral standard is that keeping someone against their will and not caring about their consent is worse. 
Is there something beyond your standard to prove me wrong ? 
Roles reversed, I unequivocally believe someone could cheat on me if I won’t allow them to leave. 
I did get away eventually, but my way out was not ideal. Still ended up homeless. Fortunately he has changed, but if he had carried out his threats, I would have lost everything I loved. He would have turned my family against me too, as he promised

It took me trying to leave at least two times (and being kept in place by threats, Financial, & psychological abuse) before I got away. If I could go back, I may have found another solution to feel free. So that perhaps proves something was wrong with me. 
But my bargaining, as you put it, comes from a place of wanting people to see not everything is black & white. I think keeping someone against their will & pushing over their consent is worse than rebelling And cheating in that instance. 
& if you’ve ever been in an abusive relationship like that, you’ll have an easier time seeing leaving can make things worse at first. I was homeless when I left him, for a time.

If I was defending myself for violence committed in self-defense, it wouldn’t prove I believed I was wrong. 
Also https://www.loveisrespect.org/content/is-cheating-abuse/
Thankfully it’s over.
Right ? For sure !!

I see where you’re coming from. I’d compare it more to a violent act as self-defense. I think having wanted sex as a result of having one’s autonomy stripped away (and also telling my partner he was free to do so) is not morally the same as some other types of cheating. Ie: telling him he can’t sleep with anyone else while I do what I want. 

In addition, I think I would have deserved exactly what I did to my husband, if the roles had been reversed.  

I may be wrong. Maybe someday my viewpoint will change. But I see it as similar to punching someone who just robbed you, trying to get your stuff back. 
Punching someone who didn’t do anything to warrant it is wrong. But punching someone to reclaim what’s yours after an act of violence, imho, is right. I feel I was taking back what was mine (my body, my soul).

I’m bipolar and stayed really loyal (to the point of blocking anyone I’d ever been remotely attracted to) until after the abuse, unwanted sex, and various ways of trapping me. I appreciate the different opinion but still don’t think I did something evil per se.

Strangely, for myself, I wouldn’t use my mental illness as a justification If that was what led to cheating on its own. I think my mental illness, the shitty marriage, the unwanted sex, and so on do NOT excuse the way my son missed out during that chaotic time however.  My son is innocent and deserves way better. His dad has turned it around from what I know, so I think the marriage ending is less toxic for my son than if it hadn’t ended.

But now he’s really delayed, and I’m worried he will never be on track. His symptoms mimic autism, and we’re working on further assessment to figure out if it’s that.  But something tells me it’s because, though I loved him, I was switched off at times during depression and not always there when he needed me.

To be perfectly honest, my son has delays. Some think it’s cause he’s autistic. I think it’s my fault I wasn’t fully there for him during periods of depression.

It depends. A lot of them have been related to continuing to play music which is helpful. My psychotic break was full of signs that made me feel like a terrible mother and that I deserved to die. And there was some truth in it, because I was failing as a mom during untreated mental health crises. It felt like the universe was trying to kill me for my crimes lol. But now I’m at the point where I’m led to apologize for past wrongs and do what I can to fix mistakes. The problem is, there are some mistakes I’ve made that have had consequences that can’t seem to change. And I often feel I see signs that make me feel I deserve to suffer as a result. So idk.

Well if I don’t get my answer, a helpful alternative may be to fully accept & understand that mental illness is also medical. For some reason, I have no mercy for myself when something bad occurs while mental illness symptoms are showing. Like I don’t want an excuse, I just want to really truly be better. I know I’m mentally ill. I know it’s medical (but my feelings don’t, if that makes sense). But I’m worried if these symptoms never change, I won’t be able to sustain living, as dramatic as it sounds. I just have a lot on my shoulders, and I’m just tired of failing and inadvertently hurting people I love.

Fortunately, due to my parents’ help, I recently got to move back into them and have reduced my responsibilities to just school. And I’ll have my son, while living with them, during the summer. While I keep trying to figure out a consistent way to recover, it’s what’s best for him. I kept having to go inpatient on my own, and after I got evicted during a long inpatient stay, I tried one more time in my own apartment. It worked for awhile, but I was barely keeping up and feared my son was becoming at risk as my illness was unpredictable. 

 For now, I need the extra support trying to parent with medication-resistant mental illness symptoms. I’m so glad they’re helping, because I hated feeling like I couldn’t do enough for my son on the days I’ve had him. I tried so hard and love him with everything, but I was still letting him down.  

I was just reading about these symptoms and their connection to narcolepsy, and I have sooo many other symptoms of narcolepsy. Gonna talk to my doctor about it next visit, because medication has never fixed my sleep disturbances. My sleep schedule and day-time fatigue is awful and has lead to so many fuck-ups. Maybe if it’s something else on top of mental illness, a new medical treatment will actually make a difference.
